title: Ramp Launch Collision Lab
description: A physics collision laboratory where the user builds a ramp to launch a ToyCar off an elevated platform into a CesiumMilkTruck parked below. The user adjusts ramp angle, launch height, surface friction, initial push force, gravity strength, and restitution coefficient, then launches the car and observes the resulting collision with momentum transfer, knockback, and energy readouts.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a ramp-launch collision physics lab. Load both shared_assets/ToyCar.glb and shared_assets/CesiumMilkTruck.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: a ground plane with grid texture, a raised platform on the left side (height adjustable), a ramp surface connecting the platform edge downward, and the CesiumMilkTruck parked stationary on the ground to the right as the collision target. Place the ToyCar at the top of the ramp. Use OrbitControls for camera, starting at a side-view angle. Add ambient light (0.5) and a directional light with shadows enabled. Create a dat.GUI or HTML control panel with these parameters: (1) Ramp Angle slider 15-60 degrees, default 30, (2) Platform Height slider 1-5 meters, default 3, (3) Surface Friction slider 0.0-1.0, default 0.2, (4) Push Force slider 5-50 N, default 20, (5) Gravity slider 5-20 m/s², default 9.8, (6) Restitution (bounciness) slider 0.0-1.0, default 0.5. Add a Launch button and a Reset button. Validate all parameters are within range before launch. On launch, animate the ToyCar sliding down the ramp using simplified physics: apply gravity component along ramp minus friction, compute velocity at ramp exit, then projectile motion through the air until it hits the ground or the truck. On collision with the MilkTruck, apply momentum transfer: the truck should slide backward proportional to the car's impact velocity and mass ratio. Apply restitution to determine bounce. Display a HUD overlay showing: current car velocity, kinetic energy at impact (0.5mv²), momentum transferred, and max height achieved during flight. The truck's knockback distance should be shown after collision settles. Use requestAnimationFrame for smooth animation. Both models should cast and receive shadows. Add a faint trajectory trail line behind the car during flight using a BufferGeometry line that updates each frame.
